headline: 5th annual Glass City JazzFest concludes August 14–15 run — dual-venue weekend concurrent with Toledo Pride; post-event figures expected
paragraphs: The 5th annual Glass City JazzFest announced its 2026 lineup on July 1. The two-day festival returns August 14–15: the evening of August 14 at the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater (doors 5 p.m., performances 6–10:30 p.m.; $10 advance general admission, $20 advance reserved seating, $20 day-of general admission; free parking on Broadway Street), followed by a free all-day session August 15 at Glass City Metropark (1–10:30 p.m.), the signature riverside venue on the Glass City Riverwalk corridor. TARTA operates transit service to the event. A post-festival Jazz Jam at Assembly Downtown Kitchen and Bar (Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Toledo) runs 10:30 p.m.–1:30 a.m. Saturday night.

The 2026 lineup includes Toledo native saxophonist Mike Williams, pianist Bob Baldwin, and vocalist Lindsey Webster. WTOL noted that the 5th edition looks 'a little different' in its format compared to prior years, though specific changes beyond the dual-venue structure have not been detailed publicly as of this brief.

As of August 9 — five days before the festival's August 14 opening at the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater — no weather alerts, logistics changes, or ticket sellout notices have been announced. The dual-venue format places a ticketed cultural draw at the Toledo Zoo and a zero-barrier crowd day at Glass City Metropark on the same mid-August weekend. The Metropark's free Saturday is the economic activation element: it brings thousands of visitors to the riverfront without a ticket price threshold, generating foot traffic for Maumee riverside restaurants and vendors.

As of August 11 — three days before the August 14 opening — Glass City JazzFest is now the immediate next major economic activation event on Toledo's summer calendar, following Toledo Jeep Fest's conclusion on August 9. No weather advisories, logistics changes, or ticket sellout notices have been announced. Free parking and TARTA shuttle service are available from 20 Main St. (by DOCKS restaurants) for Saturday's Glass City Metropark session. The full lineup — Toledo native saxophonist Mike Williams, pianist Bob Baldwin, and vocalist Lindsey Webster — appears across both venues. TLCHD has not issued any health advisories in connection with the festival.

As of August 12 — two days before the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater opening — Glass City JazzFest is imminent. No weather advisories, capacity changes, or logistics disruptions have been announced as of this brief. The Saturday, August 15 free session at Glass City Metropark (1–10:30 p.m.) is the economic activation anchor: zero barrier to entry brings foot traffic to the riverfront that supports the attendance case for the Maumee riverside corridor. Detroit-based vocalist Michon Young is confirmed for Saturday's Metropark stage alongside the full lineup from both nights. TARTA bus service to the event and free parking at 20 Main St. remain available for Saturday. Advance tickets for Friday's Zoo Amphitheater show remain available at ticketleap.com.

As of August 13 — the day before the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater opening — Glass City JazzFest opens tomorrow. Doors open at 5 p.m. Friday, August 14, at the Zoo Amphitheater (performances 6–10:30 p.m.); advance tickets remain available at ticketleap.com ($10 general admission advance, $20 reserved advance, $20 day-of general admission). No weather advisories, logistics changes, or ticket sellout notices have been announced as of this brief. The free Saturday all-day session at Glass City Metropark (August 15, 1–10:30 p.m.) follows the next day — the riverfront economic activation anchor — with free parking at 20 Main St. and TARTA bus service available. Detroit-based vocalist Michon Young and the full lineup of Toledo native saxophonist Mike Williams, pianist Bob Baldwin, and vocalist Lindsey Webster are confirmed across both venues. A post-festival Jazz Jam runs 10:30 p.m.–1:30 a.m. at Assembly Downtown Kitchen and Bar (Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Toledo).

Glass City JazzFest's 5th annual edition opens tonight, August 14, at the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater — the ticketed evening that anchors the two-day festival. Doors open at 5 p.m.; performances run 6–10:30 p.m. with Toledo native saxophonist Mike Williams, pianist Bob Baldwin, and vocalist Lindsey Webster headlining. A post-show Jazz Jam at Assembly Downtown Kitchen and Bar (Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Toledo) runs 10:30 p.m.–1:30 a.m. The free all-day Saturday session at Glass City Metropark follows tomorrow, August 15, from 1–10:30 p.m. — the economic activation anchor of the weekend, when a zero-barrier entry brings thousands of visitors to the Maumee riverside corridor. Detroit-based vocalist Michon Young joins the full lineup Saturday. Free parking at 20 Main St. and TARTA bus service are available for the Saturday Metropark session. Toledo Pride 2026 is running concurrently this same weekend (August 14–16) at Promenade Park downtown, making this the highest-concentration downtown economic activation weekend of Toledo's 2026 summer calendar.

Glass City JazzFest Day 2 — the signature free all-day session at Glass City Metropark — is underway on August 15, running 1–10:30 p.m. Detroit-based vocalist Michon Young joins the full lineup of Toledo native saxophonist Mike Williams, pianist Bob Baldwin, and vocalist Lindsey Webster at the Maumee riverside venue. Free parking at 20 Main St. and TARTA bus service are active. Toledo Pride 2026's main Saturday is running concurrently: the Toledo Pride Parade stepped off at noon at 13th and Adams, moving down Adams Street to Summit Street to Promenade Park, where 'Pride at Promenade' runs noon to 10 p.m. No weather advisories have been issued for either event. Attendance figures for Glass City JazzFest and Toledo Pride are expected to be published in the days following the weekend.

The 5th annual Glass City JazzFest concluded its full two-day run on August 15, 2026. The ticketed August 14 evening at the Toledo Zoo Amphitheater and the free all-day Saturday at Glass City Metropark both ran without disruption; the dual-venue format delivered the dual economic activation — a ticketed cultural draw at the Zoo and a zero-barrier riverfront crowd day at the Metropark — that organizers and Metroparks Toledo designed it to deliver. Toledo Pride 2026 ran concurrently across all three days (August 14–16) at Promenade Park, making the August 14–15 window the highest-concentration simultaneous downtown and riverfront economic activation of Toledo's 2026 summer calendar. Post-event attendance figures for Glass City JazzFest are expected from Metroparks Toledo and Destination Toledo in the coming days; economic impact estimates typically follow within a week.
why_it_matters: Now in its 5th year, Glass City JazzFest is one of the Metropark system's most established mid-summer events and a direct test of the 'completed Riverwalk section as event attractor' thesis. Free attendance at Glass City Metropark on August 15 creates a no-barrier crowd day for the riverfront that supports the foot-traffic arguments Toledo EDOs and mixed-use developers near the corridor use in their investment cases. The dual-venue model — pairing a ticketed evening at the Zoo Amphitheater with a free riverfront day — also demonstrates the Metroparks-Toledo Zoo programming partnership maturing as a regional event-calendar anchor.
